title: Housing needs, solar power and road safety
subtitle: Parks plan, parking penalty system, well drilling contracts, business park house demolition and Belwood Hall grant application.
overview: Council received the Housing Needs Assessment and directed staff to report back on future housing initiatives by September 29, 2025 {{vote:m2}}. It also approved the 2025 Parks and Recreation Plan {{vote:m16}} and endorsed the Active Transportation and Mobility Plan, which starts a public review period {{vote:m9}}.

On energy and safety, Council endorsed a rooftop solar system for the new Operations Centre with an upset limit of $1.2 million {{vote:m6}}. It also approved $17,500 for four new crossing guards from September to December 2025 and endorsed intersection improvements {{vote:m7}}, and adopted a new speed by-law {{vote:m8}}.

Other decisions include approving demolition of the house and shed in the Business Park, subject to a designated substance audit {{vote:m4}}. Council awarded two well-drilling contracts for Wells 3 and 7 {{vote:m14}} and set up an Administrative Monetary Penalty System for parking tickets {{vote:m17}}. Staff are expected to bring many of these items back through the 2026 budget process.

decisions.detail: Council received the report from the consultants and directed staff to report on future housing initiatives by September 29, 2025.
Council approved the 2025 Parks and Recreation Plan, including the Parks Plan and Needs Assessment.
Council endorsed the net-metered rooftop system (Option 1) and authorized competitive bids through the general contractor up to $1.2 million.
Council endorsed improvements at four intersections, approved $17,500 for four crossing guards through December 2025, and sent 2026 costs to the budget process.
Council approved demolishing the house and shed, with a designated substance audit and a full project update and budget to come back.
Council awarded the monitoring well and production well drilling tenders to two contractors and revised project funding.
Council adopted by-laws for a parking penalty system with screening and hearing officers, and authorized an agreement with the Ministry of Transportation for vehicle owner data.
Council endorsed the plan, directed a Notice of Study Completion, and asked staff to bring its projects forward in budget deliberations.

debate: On the housing report, one councillor questioned the recommended agricultural workers housing study, asking whether the local farm base warranted it and whether a broader review of rental and purpose-built housing was needed. The consultant said seasonal worker housing is poorly documented and the study was only a suggestion to explore.

Councillors asked what 'attainable' housing means compared with 'affordable'. The consultant and staff said the province has no clear definition of attainable, and the recommendation is to adopt the provincial affordable definition in the next Official Plan.

One councillor said the housing report may already be dated given recent additions, rentals and short-term rentals, and wanted more focus on seniors housing. Staff said they would look at a role for the Township and the federal Housing Accelerator Fund.

On solar, one councillor asked whether the $1.2 million upset limit should be lowered since Option 1 costs were estimated well below that. Staff preferred to keep it because of the contract structure and limited contingency, and said any unused funds would return to their sources.

On the well-drilling tenders, a councillor asked why so few bids were received. Staff said the work is highly specialized, few contractors have the equipment, and the selected contractors are experienced.
